lines.trans: So, the defendant was kissing Sasha in the storage room.
Precisely, he was only kissing!
An ordinary kiss does not constitute infidelity!
Is that so, darling? Well, if that is how it is!
Nastya, that is enough already, stop immediately!
I take all my words back!
I agree, a kiss is real infidelity.
Your Honor, I have an important question.
Victoria, are you sure that they were kissing?
Maybe they were simply sitting next to each other?
What if she was taking a speck out of his eye?

examples.trans: A plot next to Grigory Soprykin.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'suddenly, what if', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: В комнату вдруг входит грозная Марина.
examples.trans: Formidable Marina suddenly enters the room.

examples.text: Если бы меня вдруг не стало?
examples.trans: If I were suddenly gone?

examples.text: На кухне люди начали вдруг пропадать.
examples.trans: People have suddenly started disappearing in the kitchen.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'she', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: И она сразу сказала мне да!
examples.trans: And she immediately said yes to me!

examples.text: Зачем ты кидаешь в меня макаронами?
examples.trans: Why are you throwing macaroni at me?

examples.text: Папа, а если бы она тебе отказала?
examples.trans: Dad, and what if she had turned you down?

доставать.gloss: to reach; to take out, to get

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'ставать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to reach; to take out, to get', paired with 'достать'.

examples.text: Вдруг она доставала соринку из его глаза?
examples.trans: What if she was taking a speck out of his eye?

examples.text: Не достаёт до пола?
examples.trans: He can't reach the floor?

examples.text: Ребёнок ещё не достаёт до верхней полки.
examples.trans: The child can't reach the top shelf yet.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'оринка'). Common feminine noun meaning 'speck of dust' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Вдруг она доставала соринку из его глаза?
examples.trans: What if she was taking a speck out of his eye?

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть соринка.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always speck of dust.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'from/out of', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вы же попали в настоящий шоу-бизнес!
examples.trans: After all, you got into real show business!

examples.text: Было бы здорово, если бы за измены судили!
examples.trans: It would be great if people were put on trial for cheating!

examples.text: Потерпевшая, расскажите, что произошло тем вечером.
examples.trans: Victim, tell us what happened that evening.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'eyes' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Тебе нужно особое приглашение, Максим?
examples.trans: Do you need a special invitation, Maxim?

examples.text: Спасибо, Виктор Петрович, я согласен.
examples.trans: Thank you, Viktor Petrovich, I agree.

examples.text: Во сне я был смелым гладиатором.
examples.trans: In the dream I was a brave gladiator.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Наверное, он сейчас прямо придёт.
examples.trans: He will probably arrive right now.

examples.text: Я вчера пошёл к Елене Павловне.
examples.trans: Yesterday I went to see Elena Pavlovna.

examples.text: Сеня и Федя, готовьте закуски!
examples.trans: Senya and Fedya, prepare the snacks!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'darkness' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На складе в темноте и без штанов?
examples.trans: In the storage room in the dark and without pants?

examples.text: В темноте ничего не видно.
examples.trans: Nothing can be seen in the dark.

examples.text: Давай резко напугаем его в темноте!
examples.trans: Let us suddenly scare him in the dark!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Шеф сегодня ещё не приходил?
examples.trans: Has the Chef not arrived yet today?

examples.text: Наверное, он сейчас прямо придёт.
examples.trans: He will probably arrive right now.

examples.text: Я сделал ей нормальное предложение.
examples.trans: I made her a proper marriage proposal.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'without', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: На складе в темноте и без штанов?
examples.trans: In the storage room in the dark and without pants?

examples.text: Это без проблем.
examples.trans: That's no problem.

examples.text: В этот раз без обмана.
examples.trans: This time there's no trick.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'pants, trousers' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На складе в темноте и без штанов?
examples.trans: In the storage room in the dark and without pants?

examples.text: Значит, штаны просто-напросто сами могли упасть!
examples.trans: That means the pants could have simply fallen down by themselves!

examples.text: Штаны слишком длинные.
examples.trans: The pants are too long.
